subject: Joint modelling of longitudinal data and binary data. The estimation using stan is not good.

messages.author: 7abd472d414d0972
messages.subject: Joint modelling of longitudinal data and binary data. The estimation using stan is not good.
parts:
Hi,

I am using rstan to jointly model the longitudinal data Y_{ij} and binary data E_i. The stan file looks as follows:


parameters {
  vector[3] beta;
  vector[3] alpha;
  real gamma0;
  vector[N2] U;
  real<lower=0> tau_e;
  real<lower=0> tau_u;
}
transformed parameters {
  real mu[N1];
  real eta[N2];
  real<lower=0> sig_e;
  real<lower=0> sig_u;

  sig_e <- sqrt(1/tau_e);
  sig_u <- sqrt(1/tau_u);

  for (i in 1:N1)
      mu[i] <- X[i] * beta + W[i] * U;
  
  for (i in 1:N2)
      eta[i] <- Xe[i] * alpha + gamma0 * U[i];

}
model {
  tau_e ~ uniform(0, 1000);
  tau_u ~ uniform(0, 1000);
  gamma0 ~ normal(0, 1000);

  for(i in 1:3){
    beta[i] ~ normal(0, 1000);
    alpha[i] ~ normal(0, 1000);
  }

  for(i in 1:N2){
    U[i] ~ normal(0, sig_u);
    E[i] ~ bernoulli_logit(eta[i]);
  }

  for (i in 1:N1)
    Y[i] ~ normal(mu[i], sig_e);

}


I generated data from this model using true alpha -0.2, 0.2, -0.1, true beta 0.2, 0.3, 0.1, true "gamma0" 5, true standard deviation of random effect U 0.3 and true standard deviation of measurement error for Y_{ij} 0.3.
At first I generated 200 subjects, each has 6 repeated measurements of Y as well as a binary outcome E, the result looks very good and stan ran very fast. But when I decrease the sample size to 36 subjects. The beta estimation is still good, however the estimation for alpha and gamma0 is way off. Also it runs considerably(several hours) longer than the 200 subjects case. The output is as below:

Is there anything I did wrong? I executed the stanfile using the following command:


fit <- stan(file = "simmodel.stan", data = c("N1", "N2", "Y" ,"E" ,"X",

                                          "W", "Xe"), 

            iter = 5000, chains = 4, cores = 4, 

            control = list(max_treedepth = 15))

            

I also tried this same sample size -- 36 subjects with JAGS and it behaves much better than Stan so I was confused how to improve stan's performance for this "small" sample size?

Any help is appreciated!

If the models are the same, Stan and JAGS should give you
the same answer if both converge and mix well.

It looks from your print() statement above that Stan's fitting
the model OK.

Were you surprised at values like -400 and 300? Maybe you shouldn't
be with a normal(0, 1000) prior and not much data. Did JAGS
converge to the same answer? Did it mix well (using our
posterior analysis, which is much more conservative than JAGS's
in cases that don't mix well)?

- Bob
